newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila wheat buyers scared away by peso fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila wheat buyers scared away by peso fall.

text.p: Philippine wheat importers, concerned about the drop of the peso to a record low on Monday, were expected to stay away from the market despite softer U.S. wheat prices, Manila grains traders said.
"The peso fall will definitely temper our buying intentions," an executive in a Philippine flour mill told Reuters.
Philippine flour mills flocked to the U.S. wheat market last week after prices fell on a report by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
In the report on Tuesday, the USDA raised its estimate of 1997/98 U.S. wheat production to 68.87 million tonnes, up more than 2.50 million in 1996/1997.
U.S. wheat prices dropped following the announcement, prompting Philippine wheat buyers to buy up to 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat in three separate transactions last week, traders said.
On Friday, Philippine mills bought at auction 30,000 tonnes of dark northern spring with 14 percent protein content and 5,000 tonnes of western white wheat, traders said.
Two other groups bought a total 65,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat last Wednesday.

"I had expected more mills to book forward orders this week because of softer U.S. wheat prices. That prospect seems to have dimmed because of the drop in the peso," a senior Manila grains trader said.
Philippine mills had stepped up wheat buying at the beginning of this month due to lower prices and the peso's slight recovery, traders said.
Local buyers had since the beginning of the month bought a total of 267,000 tonnes of wheat, including 100,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat. This included last week's transactions, traders said.
Philippine wheat buyers were mostly sidelined last month after the peso plunged more than 11 percent after its de facto devaluation on July 11.
The peso slumped to a record low 30.10 against the dollar in early trade on Monday against the previous close of 29.80.
